facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons contain locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales as a subset of the wider Index Polygon database.
The dataset is divided into separate files for each local authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both authority files.
The current download page states that the dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
New files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
The current authority list includes London Borough of Haringey with a GML download entry.
HM Land Registry supplies GML as an open standard usable across GIS and CAD systems.
The polygons are captured against British National Grid coordinates.
The guidance warns that BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can shift features by up to 15 metres.
The index map covers registered titles and pending applications for first registration.
A form SIM result identifies whether land is registered, affected title numbers and the registration type disclosed.
Accepted search spatial data must use supported formats and OSGB 1936 British National Grid.
Supplement 6 describes searches of the index map as a plan-related service.
The guide identifies Electronic Extent Data polygons as another plan-related service.
HM Land Registry states that it provides factual information and impartial procedural advice.
The National Polygon Dataset specification states that an index polygon provides an indicative location index for a registered title.
The title plan and register record the general position of boundaries unless an exact boundary is determined.
The specification includes mandatory Shape, Poly_ID and Title_No fields.
The live Air Quality Management Area page reports 498 areas.
The dataset reports one provider and authoritative-source origin.
AQMAs are considered in plan-making and development-management decisions.
The live AONB page reports 34 areas.
The dataset reports two providers and authoritative-source origin.
AONBs are designated by Natural England and inform protected-site planning guidance.
The live Asset of Community Value page reports 101 records.
Listing an asset of community value is also a Local Land Charge.
Some planning authorities may treat ACV listing as a material consideration for change-of-use applications.
The live Brownfield Land page reports 37,671 records.
The dataset reports 354 providers and authoritative-source origin.
The register supports planning policy, development-site identification and investment transparency.
The live Building Preservation Notice page reports 9 records.
A BPN takes effect immediately and protects the building temporarily as if listed.
The current data is MHCLG-created and marked for replacement by authoritative data.
The live Special Area of Conservation page reports 260 areas.
SACs protect specific habitats and species following DEFRA designation advice.
The live Ramsar page reports 73 sites.
Ramsar sites are internationally protected wetlands of international importance.
The live National Park page reports 10 administrative boundaries.
The page describes the data as ONS-provided administrative boundaries for statistics.
The live Special Protection Area page reports 88 areas.
SPAs are designated for protection of birds and wildlife and are supplied by Natural England.
The live Heritage Coast page reports 32 areas.
A heritage coast is defined by agreement between maritime local authorities and Natural England.
The live Nutrient Neutrality Catchment page reports 39 catchments.
The catchments are designated by Natural England.
The Nature Improvement Area page reports 12 areas.
The current data is MHCLG-created and marked for authoritative replacement.
The Planning Data API accepts latitude and longitude and returns entities whose geometry intersects the point.
Multiple dataset parameters may be supplied in one coordinate query.
The documentation warns that no returned result does not prove absence because coverage varies by area.
The dataset index lists 56 geography datasets.
Title boundary is included among the geography datasets.
Datasets are grouped by typologies including geography, category, legal instrument, document, organisation, policy, metric and timetable.
The 10 metre DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
It is resampled from the 2 metre DTM using bilinear interpolation.
The composite favours the newest best-resolution survey where repeat coverage exists.
The 2 metre DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
It includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and the terrain surface.
The page reports surveys from 2000 to 2022 and vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The 2 metre first-return DSM uses the first or only laser return.
It is derived from National LIDAR Programme surveys captured from 2016 to 2022.
It is supplied as 5 kilometre GeoTIFF tiles aligned to the OS grid and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The 25 centimetre composite DTM is retired and no longer available on the platform.
The page states that it was replaced by the 1 metre composite.
The full archive still includes 25 centimetre time-stamped data.
The LIDAR Composite Catalogues dataset describes indices for full-coverage LIDAR surveys of England.
The page currently reports no data services or resources.
The catalogue metadata records creation and revision on 11 September 2023.
OS Terrain 5 provides a 5 metre grid and 5 metre interval contour product from common source data.
GML feature identifiers follow an os.t5 tile-and-sequence structure and are regenerated on whole-tile refresh.
The GML coordinate reference system is expressed as EPSG 27700.
The grid GML carries metadata while spatial heights are held in the external ASCII data block.
Each 5 kilometre tile contains 1,000 rows of 1,000 five-metre pixels.
Grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.01 metre.
Per-tile XML metadata follows the GEMINI standard.
Metadata includes tile version, reason for change and lineage status.
An XSLT stylesheet is provided to render XML metadata as HTML.
Contour data uses GML 3.2.1 simple-features level 0.
Software may ignore the schema, use a local copy or access the online schema.
Spot heights select a highest mass point at least one metre above a closed contour and round z to one decimal place.
Contour feature types are represented as individual features for interpretation and styling.
Contours and tidelines are rounded to two decimal places.
ContourLine types include master, ordinary and auxiliary values aligned with INSPIRE terminology.
